A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OOC prompting research, despite the changed title and theoretical framework. The complete main texts and appendices, including equations, figures, tables, and prompts, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original OOC-versus-baseline experiments on five datasets, including Tables 1–3 and predictive-performance and model-scaling results.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds original synthetic semantic-leakage experiments testing the effect of stratification in Section 5.2 and Figure 4.

M1.justification: v1 Algorithm 1 begins by estimating S with the LLM; v2 accepts S directly, retains estimation as a fallback, and uses supplied exogenous variables in Section 5.2. This generalizes the conditioning inputs. The obfuscation and context-addition prompts, randomized context selection, and majority-vote pipeline remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: The five earlier datasets remain, several under shortened names. Section 5.2 adds three controlled semantic-leakage tasks: animal preferences versus food completions, and color or food preferences versus occupation completions. Known exogenous variables and explicitly generated counterfactual inputs introduce a distinct testing scenario for individual invariance beyond the retained classification benchmarks.

E2.justification: Matched benchmark comparisons retain Default/Standard, CoT, and the same six safety prompts, including the same Amazon exclusions. The Qwen scaling study retains Default/Standard, CoT, and Precog. The new semantic-leakage study uses existing Standard and Unbiased comparators; it introduces no new comparison method.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 introduces a controlled design covering combinations of three binary exogenous variables and multiple contexts, with Claude 3.5 Sonnet generating inputs and gpt-4o-mini predicting answers. It adds CI Probability, measuring prediction agreement across counterfactual groups. The existing 200-example bias and F1 protocols remain; renaming CI_delta to SI-bias leaves their numerical computation unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a direct stratification ablation comparing OOC without supplied exogenous variables and with U1, (U1,U2), and (U1,U2,U3). Figure 4 tests whether finer conditioning approaches individual counterfactual invariance and reveals an intermediate nonmonotonic result. The earlier Qwen model-size analysis is retained in Appendix E rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: v1 explicitly identifies OOC results as means and standard deviations over three independent executions. v2 retains the same ± values but omits that explanation and run count. It additionally reports fixing seeds for the synthetic experiment. These are reporting changes, without evidence that the retained experiments used more or fewer runs.

E6.justification: All matched means and uncertainty values in Tables 1–3 are unchanged. v2 adds substantive counterfactual-invariance results: fully stratified OOC achieves CI Probability 0.75, 0.75, and 0.50 on Animal/Food, Color/Work, and Food/Work, respectively, with nonmonotonic intermediate behavior on Food/Work. It also newly summarizes the retained benchmark scores as improvements over Default in 23/27 settings.

T1.justification: v1 Proposition 1 treats conditional independence as sufficient for almost-sure counterfactual invariance, while Proposition 2 uses a counterfactual adjustment-set assumption. v2 replaces this foundation with stratified invariance, an observational equivalence under adjustment assumptions in Lemma 1, and an augmentation guarantee under context recoverability and exact conditional sampling in Theorem 1. Appendix A supplies replacement proofs; Appendix B adds graphical adjustment reasoning.

C1.justification: The central contribution shifts from OOC as a route to counterfactual-invariant predictions to a stratified-invariance framework with an observational test and test-time augmentation guarantee. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion now distinguish population guarantees from approaching individual invariance and claim empirical support for that relationship. This substantially revises the scope of the original guarantee.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the retained benchmark improvements as stratified rather than individual counterfactual invariance. It expands the existing proxy-S caveat, makes exact context recovery explicit, and identifies counterfactual conditional generation as a particularly strong LLM assumption. Section 5.2 attributes imperfect and nonmonotonic invariance to imperfect conditional sampling and explicitly distinguishes approaching individual invariance from satisfying it.

D1.justification: v2 specifies which model families use transformation temperatures 0.7 and 0.8, lists the synthetic variables in Appendix D, and adds completion and data-generation prompts in Appendix F. These are localized documentation additions. Conversely, Table 4 drops the earlier task-specific Z_list column although Prompt 13 still requires it. The temperature clarification does not establish a change to retained experimental settings.

R1.justification: v2 substantially repositions the work around distinctions between observational, stratified, and counterfactual fairness. It adds substantive engagement with Fawkes and Evans, Silva, Quinzan and colleagues, and Plecko and Bareinboim, and revises its interpretation of Veitch and colleagues. Earlier proxy-measurement references are removed, while semantic-leakage literature supports the new experimental direction.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, contribution statements, theoretical exposition, method explanation, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Results are divided into real-world and synthetic studies; scaling moves to an appendix; the appendices are reorganized around proofs, adjustment choices, synthetic tasks, results, and prompts. Terminology also changes from explicit to implicit safety instructions and from Default to Standard prompting.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the introductory OOC diagram, replaces main-text result tables with stacked improvement plots, and replaces dataset-specific F1 scatterplots with model-specific boxplots. Retained tables and scaling plots are relocated and reformatted. It adds the stratification-results plot and causal DAG figure, and converts the earlier prompt-parameter figure into Table 4.

improvement.justification: v1's Proposition 1 and Appendix A treat distributional evidence as establishing almost-sure counterfactual invariance. v2 corrects this central mismatch through stratified invariance and appropriately scoped observational and augmentation results with proofs. The controlled stratification study and clearer assumptions strengthen the connection between claims and evidence. Losing the three-run uncertainty explanation and Z_list parameter values weakens reproducibility, but these limited losses do not outweigh the substantial improvement in the validity and calibration of the central guarantee.
